I just updated my own RStan to 2.8.2 and everything worked fine.
But then I don't have much in my R environment other than RStan
and ggplot2.

All I did was what the instructions said here:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started

I started from what was presumably a good state of my Makevars.

Then I just followed along cutting-and-pasting:

> Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS = "-j4")

> install.packages("rstan", dependencies = TRUE)

> quit()

restart R

> library(rstan)

... everything worked fine in 2.8.2 here ...


Did you all set "dependencies=TRUE"? If so, and you were sure to exit all running
R processes and restart, could you let us know what's in your Makevars file in
the R install directory?

- Bob

I'm running into a similar issue on Mac. When I build from source, I run into this error:
** testing if installed package can be loaded
Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
  unable to load shared object '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/rstan/libs/rstan.so':
  /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/rstan/libs/rstan.so: undefined symbol: _ZN4stan4lang15indexes_grammarIN5boost6spirit17line_pos_iteratorIN9__gnu_cxx17__normal_iteratorIPKcSsEEEEEC1ERNS0_12variable_mapERSt18basic_stringstreamIcSt11char_traitsIcESaIcEERNS0_18expression_grammarISA_EE
Error: loading failed

This error is reproducible with the following dockerfile:
FROM ubuntu:14.04


RUN echo "deb http://cran.rstudio.com/bin/linux/ubuntu trusty/" >> /etc/apt/sources.list
RUN apt-key adv --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys E084DAB9


RUN DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        libcurl4-openssl-dev \
        libxml2-dev \
        gfortran \
        g++ \
        r-base-dev=3.2.3-1trusty0


RUN echo "r <- getOption('repos'); r['CRAN'] <- 'https://cran.rstudio.com/'; options(repos=r)" >> ~/.Rprofile
RUN Rscript -e "Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS='-j4'); install.packages('rstan', dependencies=TRUE)"

messages.subject: Re: Stan fit error (init_adapt.hpp: No such file or directory)
parts:
On Tuesday, January 5, 2016 at 10:52:15 AM UTC-5, Bill Lattner wrote:
Installing StanHeaders 2.8.0 prior to installing rstan fixes the issue I pointed out above. Would it make sense to pin the exact version of this dependency (instead of " >= 2.8.0")?

Not really. It hasn't happened yet, but at some point we may have to do patch releases to StanHeaders that fix bugs but are not incompatible with the existing version of rstan. But even if we did, you would have to manually install the previous StanHeaders to get it to work with the current rstan on days like today. Just doing install.packages("rstan", dependencies = TRUE) won't grab StanHeaders 2.8.x if 2.9.0 is available from whatever mirror you are downloading from.

If you need something today, then there are workarounds like installing the old StanHeaders or installing the new rstan from GitHub. Otherwise, the new rstan will be on the main CRAN website this afternoon hopefully and on your CRAN mirror sometime this week.

Ben
